text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Joining Europe's Economic and Monetary Union would be a leap to the unknown, says interim report from government appointed EMU committee of leading economics professors, which plans to give a recommendation in May.
- Turku's Turun Palloseura (TPS) and Helsinki's Jokerit to meet in national ice-hockey finals. The first leg to be played on Thursday in Turku.
- Only one in five Finns are able to find help from public sector services, study shows.
- Representatives for Finland and Sweden to meet NATO officials on Wednesday to assess the results and objectives of expanded cooperation between NATO and the non-aligned Nordic countries.

- Silja expects significant growth in traffic between Finland and Estonia after visa requirements are lifted in May, plans to move its large Finnjet passenger ferry to the Helsinki-Tallinn route next winter from Helsinki-Lubeck.
- Local governments to compile their first budgets in euros in 2002, says Arto Laitinen finance director at the Federation of Finnish local authorities.
- Finland, currently chairing the European Council, proposes a human rights ombudsman for the council.
- Trade unions' joint statement on EMU -- due by summer -- is progressing slowly, union sources say.
- Young fishermen coming from outside the sector have developed the industry with creative entrepreneurial ideas, study shows.
- It would be possible to build wind power units producing some 250 megawatts of electricity in Lapland, says Jouni Kaas, managing director of Tuulivoima Oy.
- Ecological farming methods are becoming increasingly popular in Finland, now used on five percent of farm land.
- Rich people in Finland are elderly and often Swedish-speaking, Statistics Finland welfare study based on 1994 data shows.

- Court rejected small investors' claims for compensation for misleading information on Kansallis-Osake-Pankki's share issue before it merged with Unitas to form Merita, but did rule some information was misleading, records show.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Employers oppose tighter laws against tax fraud which would make it possible to charge employers for not paying tax advances or social contributions.
- Private entrepreneurs would suffer from reduced tax exemptions on voluntary pension insurance saving planned by finance ministry, lobby says.
- Advertising revenue rose a less-than-expected 2.7 percent to 4.6 billion markka last year, estimates show.
- The value of real estate deals made last year rose five percent to 14.3 billion markka, with the number of trades up 23 percent at 13,000, National Survey Board says.
- U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley expects Finland's Gross Domestic Product to rise 4.5 percent this year.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Insurers' and taxpayers' lobbies are defending voluntary pension insurance tax exemptions.
- National carrier Finnair does not expect abolished restrictions on domestic air traffic to have any rapid impact in Finland, saying Finland's small volumes make it unattractive to foreign airlines.
- Finland's high unemployment caps domestic demand, keeps imports in check and thus helps maintain the exceptional current account surplus, economists say.
DEMARI
- A Swedish-Finnish currency union is not an alternative to EMU, says Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen.
